clue.text: City of London

parts.note: read as the first word of a London district's name: the colour that goes before 'City' in a west London place

explanation.surface: A one-line definition of the Square Mile, London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City of London' looks like the Square Mile, but the clue wants the word that completes White City, a district of west London once home to BBC Television Centre.
explanation.definitionFit: White City is a London district, so the colour word is the one that makes a London 'City'.

clue.text: Taylor was not of the Lakeland fraternity

definitions.text: Taylor was not of the Lakeland fraternity

parts.words: Taylor was not of the Lakeland fraternity
parts.note: John Taylor, a Thames boatman who wrote verse, was not one of Wordsworth's circle of Lake District writers

explanation.surface: A remark that a man named Taylor did not belong to the Lake District group.
explanation.walkthrough: John Taylor (1578-1653), a Thames waterman who wrote verse, was nicknamed the Water Poet; he was a poet of water but not one of the Lake Poets, Wordsworth and his circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the boatman versifier John Taylor, who was no Lake Poet.

clue.text: Such was the tower of Stoke Poges church

definitions.text: Such was the tower of Stoke Poges church

parts.words: Such was the tower of Stoke Poges church
parts.note: Gray's Elegy, set in that Buckinghamshire churchyard, speaks of the 'ivy-mantled tower'

explanation.surface: A description of a village church tower in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' is set at Stoke Poges and mentions 'yonder ivy-mantled tower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower mantled in ivy is overgrown with that climbing plant, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: One of the first garden irrigators ?

definitions.text: One of the first garden irrigators ?

parts.words: One of the first garden irrigators
parts.note: Genesis says a river went out of Eden to water the garden and split into four heads

explanation.surface: An early device or person for watering gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first garden' is Eden; Genesis names four rivers watering it, and this is one, now flowing through Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is one of the four rivers Genesis says watered the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Lopped avenue ?

parts.note: an avenue of trees cut down to bare stems, and also a main highway between towns

explanation.surface: An avenue of trees that has had its branches cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Lopped trees are left as bare trunks, so a 'lopped avenue' is all trunks; in Britain a main road for long-distance traffic is called by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A main highway for through traffic is named after the trunk of a tree, the bare part left after lopping.

clue.text: Seesaws

parts.note: a verb here: rocks up and down, wavers unsteadily

explanation.surface: A single word naming a playground plank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seesaws' looks like the plural noun but is the verb, to wobble back and forth; in America a seesaw is also called a teeter.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to sway unsteadily up and down, the same action as to wobble on the verge.

clue.text: Pan lutes in ruins

indicators.note: lutes in ruins are smashed to pieces, so the letters are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: The god Pan reduces some lutes to wreckage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like the Greek god of music; it is a cooking pan. 'ruins' rearranges LUTES and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan is a kitchen implement, one example of a cooking tool.

clue.text: No highbrow homage

parts.note: deep bowing with the forehead to the ground, so the brow is anything but high

explanation.surface: A tribute paid in a plain, unintellectual way.
explanation.walkthrough: To kotow (also spelt kowtow) is to kneel and touch the ground with the forehead in Chinese homage, so the brow is low, not high.
explanation.definitionFit: Kotow is the Chinese act of kneeling and knocking the forehead on the ground as a mark of respect.

clue.text: Unsuitable form of discussion towards a package deal?

definitions.text: Unsuitable form of discussion towards a package deal?

parts.words: Unsuitable form of discussion towards a package deal
parts.note: a debate with no fixed limits, and a parcel left unsealed at both ends would hardly do

explanation.surface: A kind of talk that does not help negotiators reach an all-in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: An open-ended discussion has no set conclusion; read literally, a package open at both ends is no use for a parcel, the pun on 'package deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-ended means having no fixed limit or conclusion, as a free-ranging debate does.

clue.text: Make shift to get out of the way

definitions.meaning: an expedient or trick used to manage
to move aside quickly to avoid something

explanation.surface: Someone shifts sharply to avoid being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a makeshift trick, and to dodge is to step aside out of harm's way.

clue.text: A bit backward in providing book design

definitions.meaning: a piece fixed at the rear end of something, as on a violin
a decorative engraving printed at the end of a chapter

explanation.surface: Someone a little slow is somehow providing the design of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a part at the back of an object and an ornament closing a printed chapter.

clue.text: Current fashion in suitings

definitions.meaning: a river, here the one forming part of the Scottish-English border
a rough woollen cloth popular for suits

explanation.surface: What is currently stylish in men's suit fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning modern; it is a noun, a flowing body of water, the River Tweed on the Scotland-England border.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is both a border river and a woollen cloth woven for suits.

clue.text: Only one to a verdict on a deceased grey mare?

definitions.text: Only one to a verdict on a deceased grey mare?

parts.words: Only one to a verdict on a deceased grey mare
parts.note: a jury may add one recommendation to its verdict; the old song's grey mare, which died, carried a whole party on its back

explanation.surface: A jury's finding on the death of an old grey horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider is an addendum a jury attaches to its verdict. In the English folk song 'Widecombe Fair' Tom Pearce's grey mare dies after carrying seven men, so she had more than one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a recommendation appended to a jury verdict and a person sitting on a horse.

clue.text: The fräulein enquired for is not here

parts.note: Else is a common German girl's name, so a young German woman
asking where someone is: 'where?'

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the young German lady and is told she is not in.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking for Else gives 'Else, where?', which runs together as a word meaning in some other place.
explanation.definitionFit: Being somewhere other than this place is the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Or turbulent onset of a river

indicators.note: turbulent water churns, so the letters around it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A river whose beginning is rough and turbulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges OR and ONSET into the name of the river of Syria and Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orontes is a river flowing through Lebanon, Syria and Turkey.

clue.text: Few as a rule

parts.note: government by a small group: the few are those who rule

explanation.surface: A remark that something is usually scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually'; read it as 'ruling', so the few are in power, government by a small elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchy is rule by a small group, from the Greek for 'few'.

clue.text: Triumvir

parts.note: one of three men sharing power, here the third partner of Octavian and Mark Antony

explanation.surface: A single-word definition: one of a ruling trio.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second Triumvirate of Rome was Octavian, Mark Antony and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus; he is the one whose name has seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepidus was a member of Rome's Second Triumvirate, a ruling trio.

clue.text: Exams over — now for idyllic pursuits !

parts.note: finished, done with
spoken examinations are orals

explanation.surface: With exams finished, students head off for country idylls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exams over' gives ORALS PAST; written in answer order it makes the rural poems or pursuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastorals are poems or pastimes idealising simple country life.

clue.text: Took us up when stigmatized and provided support

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking the word up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
branded with disgrace, so marked or stained

explanation.surface: Someone takes us up when we are disgraced and gives us support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns US into SU, followed by STAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sustained is to have held up or supported.

clue.text: Attire to give final victory at Wimbledon

definitions.text: Attire to give final victory at Wimbledon

parts.words: Attire to give final victory at Wimbledon
parts.note: a matching jumper and cardigan, and said quickly '...', taking the deciding set of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Clothing that brings a player final victory in a Wimbledon tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: A twinset is a matching jumper and cardigan; split it as 't(o) win set' and it is what a tennis player does to win the match, Wimbledon being the London tennis tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a woman's matching cardigan and sweater, a form of clothing.

clue.text: Excursion with nothing over one pound in Africa

parts.note: a short outing is a trip
zero looks like the letter O
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trip that costs next to nothing, just over a pound, in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue O sits over (above) L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, a city in North Africa.

clue.text: Sidney's likely to get stung, what's more

indicators.note: to get stung Sidney must have the stinging insects all round him, so his short name goes inside them

parts.note: being stung points to the bees that sting
Sid is the short form of Sidney

explanation.surface: Sidney is likely to be stung, and what is more, there is something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' puts SID inside BEES, the insects that would do the stinging.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides is an adverb meaning in addition, as 'what's more' does.

clue.text: The beer's tasting of wormwood

definitions.meaning: the beer is, a pale ale known in Britain as bitter
aromatic flavourings for drinks made from herbs such as wormwood

explanation.surface: A pint whose taste recalls wormwood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain bitter is a hoppy draught ale, so 'The beer's' is 'bitter's'; bitters are herbal flavourings for cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitters are herbal flavourings such as angostura, and bitter's is a British ale's name with 'is'.

clue.text: " Pupils, attend to what is said " (examiners' notice)

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils taught together
'list' is an old word for listen, as in Hamlet's 'List, list, O list!'

explanation.surface: A teacher calls the pupils to attention, with a note from the examiners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is archaic for listen; together the call to the pupils makes the published table of results in a university exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A class list is the ranked list of exam results posted by examiners.

clue.text: Sea bean ?

parts.note: a West Indian people whose name, followed by 'bean', sounds like a sea

explanation.surface: A seed that floats in on ocean currents.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea bean is a drift seed; here the Carib people plus 'bean' sounds like Caribbean, the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are a people of the West Indies who gave their name to the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Flames rise and cross line

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: flames are fires

explanation.surface: Fire leaps up and crosses a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns FIRES upwards to give the small stroke at the end of a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the short cross stroke finishing a letter's main line in type.

clue.text: Help give Tom a hand in U.S.

indicators.note: the phrase gives up the letters held within it, running from the end of Tom through hand

explanation.surface: An appeal to help Tom by lending him a hand while in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' points to a run of letters inside 'Tom a hand', giving the Nebraskan city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is a city in Nebraska, so a place in the United States.

clue.text: Last bid

parts.note: the farewell one says when leaving, as in 'bid farewell'

explanation.surface: The final offer at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last bid' looks like an auction's final offer; it is the farewell one bids at a final parting.
explanation.definitionFit: One bids adieu, a French farewell, when parting for the last time.

clue.text: Doggone return ?

parts.note: split as 're' and a mongrel word: a dog once more, and to happen again

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance at a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doggone' is an American mild oath; read 'return' as RE (again) plus a mongrel, giving a word meaning to come back again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, to come back, so it means return.

clue.text: Something that is to be done-for the better we hope

definitions.text: Something that is to be done-for the better we hope

parts.words: Something that is to be done-for the better we hope
parts.note: a task to be carried out, and a piece of surgery the patient hopes will make things better

explanation.surface: A task still to be carried out, which we hope will improve matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'done for' look like ruin; the reading wanted is a surgical procedure that, it is hoped, makes the patient better.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is both an undertaking to be carried out and surgery meant to cure.

clue.text: Bark of hogsheads offshore ?

parts.note: a dog's bay is its deep bark
taken as written
hogs are pigs, and the clue plays on the cask name too

explanation.surface: The noise made by barrels of hogs out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bay of Pigs is the inlet on Cuba's south coast where the failed 1961 invasion landed from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Pigs is a stretch of water off the Cuban shore.

clue.text: Good listening, fathomable

definitions.meaning: in good condition, healthy, as in safe and well
relating to hearing, and able to be measured for depth, as a sailor takes depth readings with a line

explanation.surface: A tidy description of a good listener whose depths can be fathomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means healthy, also concerns hearing, and to sound water is to measure its depth.
